passage:
Chetan: Good evening Sir, can I ask something about pace? 🙏
Vijay Sir: Yes, go ahead.
Chetan: The batch is on chapter 9 of mechanics and I'm still on chapter 5. Is it realistic to catch up before December?
Vijay Sir: Which chapters are unfinished?
Chetan: 6, 7 and 8 mainly.
Vijay Sir: For your paper, 7 carries less weight. Do 6 and 8 fully, read 7 lightly. Core first, extras later.
Chetan: Should I still attend every class?
Vijay Sir: Come to the ones on core topics. Send me your test scores next week and we'll adjust.
(next day)
Chetan: The school counsellor Ma'am said much the same and gave me a weekly plan.
Chetan: Thank you, Sir 👍

qa.q: Which chapters did Vijay Sir say to do fully?
What might Chetan be worried about at the start?
qa.a: Falling behind the batch and not being able to catch up before December.

qa.q: What else could Chetan do to keep the plan on track, and why?
qa.a: Keep a small weekly chart of progress and send scores as Sir suggested, so the plan can be adjusted with evidence.

qa.q: How does Chetan's question look to Vijay Sir?
qa.a: Vijay Sir sees a student asking early and honestly instead of struggling silently, so he can guide the focus and follow up on the scores.

grounding: A student asks a coaching mentor and a school counsellor about pace and gets advice to focus on core topics.

subtype: Approach: consulting a teacher or counsellor about pace [Action]
passage:
In Kalimpong, the coaching centre for the medical entrance ran out of a two-room building above a hardware shop. Tenzin had been attending for four months, and every week the pace got faster. Three chapters on Monday. Four on Thursday.

One evening after class, he waited for the mentor, Ramesh Sir, who was packing up his chalk. "Sir, is this pace realistic? I'm drowning."

Ramesh Sir sat down on a bench. "Honestly? For most students, no." He pulled out the syllabus and put ticks beside some chapters. "These carry most of the marks. These two, you can skim."

The next day, Tenzin also went to the school counsellor, Mrs. Pradhan. She helped him draw a weekly plan: core topics first, then practice tests, and a fixed Sunday rest.

Walking home past the monastery, Tenzin felt lighter than he had in weeks.

qa.q: How long had Tenzin been attending the coaching centre?
How did Tenzin feel walking home past the monastery?
qa.a: He felt lighter and relieved, after weeks of feeling that he was drowning.

qa.q: What else could Tenzin do with the advice he received?
qa.a: He could check his progress on the core topics with Ramesh Sir each month, so the plan stays realistic.

qa.q: How might Ramesh Sir have felt when Tenzin asked his question?
qa.a: Ramesh Sir probably felt glad Tenzin asked, and honest enough to admit the pace does not suit most students.

grounding: Shows a student asking a coaching mentor and a school counsellor whether the pace is realistic and getting advice to focus on core topics.

subtype: Approach: consulting a teacher or counsellor about pace [Action]
passage:
In Madrid, Bilal was in his last year of school and taking evening classes for the university entrance exam. Every week the teacher raced through more topics, and Bilal felt like he was always three chapters behind.

He stayed after class to talk to the tutor, Sofia. "Is this pace normal? I can't keep up."

Sofia smiled tiredly. "You're not the only one asking." She showed him the exam's past papers. "These four topics come up every single year. These three, almost never. Focus on the four."

The next morning, he also booked time with the school counsellor, who helped him turn Sofia's advice into a weekly plan: core topics on weekdays, one past paper on Saturday, and Sunday afternoon off.

For the first time in weeks, Bilal went to sleep without the sick feeling of being behind.

qa.q: How many topics did Sofia say come up every single year?
How had Bilal been feeling before he spoke to Sofia?
qa.a: Bilal felt anxious and overwhelmed, always three chapters behind, with a sick feeling of being behind.

qa.q: What else could Bilal ask the counsellor at the next meeting?
qa.a: He could ask how to adjust the plan if the Saturday past papers show new weak spots, so the focus stays on what matters.

qa.q: How does Bilal's question look from Sofia's side?
qa.a: Sofia seems tired but sympathetic, knowing many students feel the same and glad to point him to what matters most.

grounding: Shows a student asking a tutor and a school counsellor whether the pace is realistic and getting advice to skip less important topics and focus on the core.
